subject: Post-demo: latency & concurrency qualification synopsis and MAP
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@solstice.ai>, Rob Han <rob@solstice.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: latency & concurrency qualification synopsis and MAP

Hi Maya / Rob —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Below is a concise recap of the performance topics we committed to validate and the proposed mutual action plan (MAP) so we can get to a pilot decision quickly. I summarized the key SLO asks from your team and shaded items we flagged as follow-ups.

Summary of Solstice SLO goals (as discussed)
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 220ms for single-turn text-generation (avg prompt + 150 token output)
- Streaming: sub-100ms first-byte for streaming-enabled responses; end-to-end stream steady-state <= 300ms
- Throughput: sustain 200 qps for batched bulk inference (non-streaming) with tail latency target 500ms
- Concurrency: support 60 concurrent active streaming sessions with per-connection KV cache warm-start

Open verification items / follow-ups (action owners)
1) Exact prompt length distributions and concurrency profile (Maya) — we need a short sample corpus and a simple traffic matrix (peak, 95th, off-peak).
2) Live streaming trace capture from your staging load test (Rob) — helps us validate first-byte characteristics.
3) SLO checklist & sample driver (Redwood) — Ben/Soojin: provide a one-sheet + a checklist you can run in <48h. (attached)
4) Quantization tolerance estimate — Karthik: run the model variant through our quick regression and share token-level diffs for the top 5 prompt classes.

Proposed MAP and near-term plan
- By EOD Tue (2028-07-10): Solstice shares a 1-hour representative traffic sample + one test prompt set (Maya)
- By Wed (2028-07-11): Redwood shares instrumented streaming harness and SLO checklist; we run an initial micro-pilot and return traces (Ben / Soojin)
- By Fri (2028-07-14): Joint run with 1k QPS burst to validate autoscale and tail behavior; follow-up triage meeting to decide pilot go/no-go (All)

Attachments: solstice-slo-checklist.xlsx (one-sheet acceptance checklist), sample-stream-trace.ndjson (example trace format)

Quick asks in this email: could you confirm the sample window (UTC) you can share, and whether you have any regional restrictions for running load from our us-west cluster?

Thanks — short next step call works if you prefer to walk the MAP live.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Great, Rob — appreciate the prompt turnaround. Answering your streaming measurement question and confirming next artifacts: 

Streaming first-byte measurement
- Redwood measures first-byte at the server egress point (after our L7 proxy) by default. For parity we can add a small client-side tracer (lightweight JS shim / curl-instrumentation) so you can correlate client-received first-byte vs server-egress. We'll include the correlation guide in the harness.

What we'll deliver by Wed (2028-07-11)
- Instrumented streaming harness + runbook (how to run from your staging environment)
- SLO acceptance checklist (spreadsheet) with pass/fail columns and example thresholds — see attached one-pager (solstice-slo-checklist.xlsx)
- Quick regression report template for quantization checks (Karthik will run and fill)

Small ask: please push the sample window (CSV) to the Drive link above or reply to this thread with a secure share link. Once we have it Soojin will schedule the test run.

If you're free Tue 2028-07-10 at 11:00am PT, let's do a 20-min technical sync to align the harness. Otherwise we'll proceed asynchronously.

Ben

I'll own the instrumented run and initial trace analysis. A couple of quick technical notes so expectations are set: 

- For the 60 concurrent streaming sessions target we recommend starting with a synthetic warm-up phase (10m) so KV caches populate — otherwise tail latency will look artificially high.
- If you can provide 2-3 representative long-prompt examples (200+ tokens) that exercise the same model paths, we'll include them in the first-byte and steady-state checks.
- We'll produce a short artifact:
  * run-trace-summary.txt (95/99/99.9 latencies, bytes-on-wire, per-session jitter)
